ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in Figure A, this is a schematic diagram of a circuit of a dimming desk lamp; it realizes stepless adjustment of brightness through a bidirectional thyristor electronic device. After the desk lamp is connected to 220 V sinusoidal alternating current, the voltage applied across the two ends of the lamp tube is as shown in Figure B. Then what is the reading of the AC voltmeter at this time?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In Figure A, the power supply is labeled as 220 V AC, and the bidirectional thyristor is connected in series with the lamp tube; the two ends of the AC voltmeter V are respectively connected to the upper and lower two nodes of the branch where the lamp tube is located, so the voltmeter is connected in parallel with the lamp tube and measures the voltage across the two ends of the lamp tube. In Figure B, the vertical axis is U/V, and the highest value marked by the dashed line is 220; the voltage waveform of the lamp tube, within each repeated half-cycle, only in the first segment presents a sinusoidal shape rising from 0 to 220 V, and the later segment is 0. Then reason: The reading of an AC voltmeter is the effective value of the measured voltage. According to Figure B and the specified method, map one repeated half-cycle to phase 0 to π, in which only 0 to π/2 has voltage, and u=220sinθ; from π/2 to π the voltage is 0. Therefore U_eff = sqrt[(1/π)∫_0^(π/2)(220sinθ)^2 dθ] = sqrt[(220^2/π)·(π/4)] = 220/2 = 110 V. Therefore the reading of the AC voltmeter at this time is 110 V.
